A Republican strategy to block Obama's re-election
The Republican leaders justified their policy by the need to fight electoral fraud.
Now, the Center Brennan considers this last one a myth and claims that the electoral fraud is less frequent in the United States than the number of people who die from lightning.
In fact, the Republican lawyers have found only 300 cases of electoral fraud in the United States in ten years.
One thing is certain: these new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In this sense, these measures will weaken the American democratic system.
In contrast to Canada, the American states are responsible for the organization of federal elections in the United States.
And in the same line, a majority of American governments have promulgated, since 2009, new laws that make the registration or voting process more difficult.
This phenomenon has spread after the November 2010 elections, which saw the increase of 675 new representatives in 26 states.
In consequence, during the year 2011, 180 bills were introduced that restricted the right to vote in 41 states.
The new electoral laws require voters to present a photo ID and a citizenship certificate, in addition to a citizenship certificate.

On the other hand, these laws reduce the periods of anticipation, invalidate the right to register as an elector on the day of the vote and remove the right to vote from citizens with criminal records.
Before the 2006 elections, no American state required voters to present a photo ID.
The State of Indiana was the first to demand it.
The Supreme Court of the United States confirmed the constitutionality of the Indiana law in 2008.
Therefore, the republican authorities rushed to extend that practice to other states.
In the last years, these authorities have supported legislation in 34 states to require voters to present a photo ID.
It is important to note that, unlike Quebec, American citizens do not have a universal identity document, such as the Social Security card.
In fact, 11% of American citizens, that is, 21 million people who are eligible to vote, do not have any photographic identification issued by a state agency.
On the other hand, five million new voters in 2012 lack a document of identity with those characteristics.
However, the cost of the required document is more than a hundred dollars.
In this way, the new restrictions affect the young, the minorities and the poor in a disproportionate way.
In fact, 25% of Afro-Americans, 15% of people who earn less than 35,000 dollars a year, 18% of citizens over 65 years old and 20% of voters between 18 and 29 years old do not have
And there is more.
In many states, the voters who vote for the candidates, the voters who can use the photo ID issued by their institution.
On the other hand, those same states authorize the clubs of fishing and hunting to use the documents issued by those clubs.
Before 2004, no state required the proof of citizenship to vote.
Arizona was the first state to present such a requirement.
Since 2011, a dozen of the states have adopted laws that require voters to show that they are American citizens.
Those measures clearly aim to limit the Hispanic vote.
It seems that two out of three Hispanics support the Democratic Party.
On the other hand, the Republican legislators supported certain laws that abolished the registration of electors on the same day of the vote in eight states.
Furthermore, they limited the right of people and groups to create a service to register voters.
These restrictions have consequences.
For example, in the 2004 general elections, the registration campaigns contributed to the registration of around 10 million citizens.
The measures taken since 2009 have resulted in the registration of new voters in 2010 compared to 2006.
In addition, the Republican legislators adopted laws in five states that favored the reduction of the period of voting in advance.
For example, in the 2008 Florida elections, 33% of the voters who voted early were African Americans, while these last represented only 13% of the voters in the state.
In the case of the Spanish, it happened exactly the same.
These represent only 11% of the voters, which is equivalent to 24% of the voters who vote in advance.
However, the whites, who represent 76% of the electorate, do not represent more than 46% of the voters who vote in advance.
Of course, the Democratic legislators and their supporters have opposed the adoption of laws that restrict the registration of voters.
In this sense, the Democratic governors have blocked several legislative projects.
The US Department of Justice intervened to suspend the most controversial laws.
It could be, in part, limited to the damage.
For example, only 16 out of 34 states have adopted the law requiring the presentation of a photo ID.
However, it is undeniable that the new rules adopted will complicate the voting rights in 2012.
The critics of the democratic party claim that the laws are part of the party's agenda, as it is clear that the laws are meant to influence the results of 2012 in the key states.
A report from the Brennan Center in 2011 shows that the states that have adopted these laws represent 171 of the 270 votes needed to achieve the presidency.
It is too early to assert with certainty whether these legislative changes at the electoral scale will have a significant impact on the results of the 2012 presidential elections.
One thing is certain: these new provisions will negatively affect the participation rate.
In this sense, the measures will weaken the American democratic system.
Detection of prostate cancer: Should one get the test or not?
In fact, the PSA test presents false results, sometimes, in some cases, false negative or false positive results, which lead to unnecessary medical interventions.
It is a reason more than enough to doubt the men, already reluctant to do the tests, about whether they should do the tests.
To take the test or not?
We have asked for advice from two experts.
In the studies conducted in the United States, a large index of infections was detected, so it is difficult to interpret those data and make firm recommendations.
In addition, the European study showed a certain mortality rate between the patients who had been detected and those who had not.
The study, with a follow-up of 12 years, showed that there is a 30 to 40% chance of having metastases if the test has not been performed.
I recommend the test starting from 50 years, or from 40 years if the father has prostate cancer.
The African-American men have a higher risk index.
The key is to make a good decision once the cancer is detected.
There are aggressive cancers and other cancers that are indifferent.

It is really necessary to make the patient understand the degree of risk of his cancer. They should be offered all possible options and not necessarily the prostate cancers that do not attack life in the long term, in which case it is better to opt for active surveillance of the disease.
Today, many men who have been diagnosed with cancer are not treated, because the cancer is not aggressive and does not pose a risk to their life.
In place of that, we suggest active monitoring of the disease and, if it progresses, we offer treatment.
We have decided to use more precise criteria to decide who should or should be treated.
I recommend that the test be done in any case.
But it is important to speak with your doctor to determine whether you should take the test or not.

Unfortunately, there is no miracle cure for cancer.
Despite the progress of the investigations, the adoption of healthy lifestyle habits remains the best way to reduce the risk of suffering from the disease.
We estimate that if everyone ate well and moved sufficiently, 30% of the cancers could be prevented.
"If no one smoked, that rate would have risen to 50%", said André Beaulieu, spokesperson for the Canadian Cancer Society.
In contrast, we evaluate that around 10% of cancers are hereditary.
Many others are completely inexplicable.
For the Canadian Cancer Society, the fight against smoking continues to be a priority despite the decrease in the number of smokers.
Tobacco is linked to 85% of the cases of lung cancer.

It greatly harms the health of the people.
"Today, still 1.5 million smokers remain in Quebec", said the spokesperson André Beaulieu.
A hopeful data: 10 years after quitting smoking, the risk of dying of cancer is reduced by half.

The food
The organization recommends, also, to limit the consumption of red meats.
In large quantities, they risk suffering from colorectal cancer.
The charcuterie products must be avoided.
The conservation of the meat for smoking, drying, or salting can cause the formation of carcinogenic substances.
"They can damage the organism and lead to the development of cancer", we explain.
The vitamins
In the last few years, several scientists have studied the links between vitamins and cancer.
However, at the moment, their investigations are not yet conclusive.
According to the SCC, the studies on vitamin E are contradictory.
While in one of them, the risk of prostate cancer was reduced, in the other, it was observed that it was increased.

The Higgs boson in detail
The announcement of the probable discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great excitement last summer, and it was for a reason.
It is believed that this boson is part of the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.
And what is more, it is the particle whose existence was predicted by the standard model: our best explanation of the nature and behavior of matter, which has not yet been observed empirically.
But for the physicists, it is not yet clear that it is Higgs.
We know that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
In addition, new data revealed in an important physics congress in Kyoto seem to confirm that it is, although more data is still needed to be completely sure.
In any case, we suppose that it is Higgs, since the chances of being wrong seem few. We will see what it is about.
In this great world, there is a general law that implies that two things cannot be found at the same time.
There is no way to violate that rule and do it too much, because it will end up hurting you.

The physicists classify the particles into two categories.
On one hand, we find the good citizens called fermions, who obey the principle of Pauli.
And there are also the anarchists, a group of anarchists who do not respect anything, or at least not this principle, which means that they can be found in the same place at the same time.

According to the Berkeley Laboratory page, "The Particle Adventure", which is extraordinary, the particles are divided into two groups: the mesons, which we will not discuss here, and the "bosons", which are the ones that the great forces of nature are related to.
These bosons, here, are not the exotic creatures that we could believe.
In fact, if he manages to read this chronicle, it is due to an extraordinary particle: the photon or the "light particle" that acts as a messenger of electromagnetic force.
In fact, when a charged particle accelerates or changes direction, it "disrupts" the electromagnetic field in that exact environment; it's like when we throw a stone into a lake.
In this "disorder" a magnetic wave (of light, infrared, ultraviolet, etc.) is born, and this wave is nothing but a photon, that is, one of the bosons "carriers of force".
The most stable field
It happens the same way with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "ordered" for this boson to appear.

Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, one needs to reach extremely high energies, just as if it were a frozen lake in which only a thick rock could slide across the surface.
Therefore, a huge accelerator like the CERN (the great particle accelerator is a 27 km ring!) is needed to reach such levels of energy.
The analogy with the electromagnetic field is a new tool that explains the relationship between the Higgs and mass.
In fact, none of the particles nor all the materials interact with the electromagnetic field.
Some, like magnets, do this, but others don't: a piece of paper, for example, will not stay stuck to the door of the fridge.
And in the same way, not all particles interact with the Higgs field: those that do have mass, while the rest (like the photon, for example), do not.

However, the European Central Bank (BCE) was interested in him in an October report on virtual currencies.
In it, the Bitcoin was described as "the most successful virtual currency", "which competes with the dollar or the euro" and "similar to conventional currencies".
Bitcoin is different from other systems with virtual currencies like "credits" used to advance in a video game and that can be won by playing or even exchanged in some cases.
The social network Facebook also developed this type of system.
But in all exchanges a central authority controls and deals with the changes.
With Bitcoin, all nodes of the network are at the same time depositaries of books, verifiers, emitters, and buyers and sellers.
How does that network work?
Each transaction between two users is made in reality between two electronic addresses in the form of electronic mail.
A user can choose a different address for each payment, ensuring anonymity.
A set of information related to this transaction is electronically signed through a double-key system.
The network can verify the authenticity of the transaction.
Thanks to the content of the file, it is also possible to ensure that the changes in bitcoins are recorded in the public book, which is spread throughout the network.
The key event consists in writing that new transaction in that book.
This is a resolution of a mathematical challenge launched at the computers and the winner will have the privilege of adding that line.
It is a phase of file fragmentation, that is, the transformation of a large file into a shorter and unique fingerprint.
The computers "take" the new transaction and add a number before "cutting" the set.
The goal is to find the number that provides a particular signature (with zeros at the beginning).
Once that number is found, the others verify easily that it is the good one.
The transaction is then inseparably linked to the chain of other transactions; any modification would change the hash.

If, in order to commit a fraud, a user wanted to pay twice with the same money very quickly (in less than ten minutes), the network would only accept one of the two transactions; the other would be left without any trace, since both have different fingerprints.
The computer that solves the challenge will be 50 bitcoins.
To prevent inflation, that reward is divided into two regularly, with probability before 2012.
The number of bitcoins in circulation is limited to 21 million, but are divisible up to the hundred million, leaving a wide margin.
The difficulty of this challenge is also revealed in each increase in computing power.

The Republican leaders justified their policy by the need to fight electoral fraud.
In conclusion, the Center Brennan considers this last as a myth and states that the electoral fraud is less frequent in the United States than the number of people killed by a lightning strike.
In fact, the Republican lawyers have found only 300 cases of electoral fraud in the United States in ten years.
One thing is certain: these new provisions will negatively affect the rate of participation.
In that sense, these measures will damage the American democratic system.
In contrast to Canada, American states are responsible for organizing federal elections in the United States.
And in the same line, a majority of American governments have promulgated, starting from 2009, new laws that make it difficult to register or vote.
This phenomenon has spread after the November 2010 elections, which saw 675 new representatives in 26 states.
As a result, 180 law projects were introduced in 2011 that restricted the right to vote in 41 states.
The new electoral laws require voters to present a photo ID and a proof of American citizenship.
On the other hand, these laws reduce the period of voting, invalidate the right to register as a voter on the day of the election and remove the right to vote from citizens with criminal records.
Before the 2006 elections, no American state required voters to present a photo ID.
Indiana State was the first to demand it.
The Supreme Court of the United States confirmed in 2008 the constitutionality of the Indiana law.
Therefore, the Republican authorities rushed to extend that practice to other states.
In recent years, these authorities have supported legislation in 34 states to require voters to present a photo ID.
It is important to note that, contrary to what happens in Quebec, American citizens do not have a universal identification document, such as the Social Security card.
In fact, 11% of American citizens, that is, 21 million people who are of voting age, do not have any photo ID issued by a government agency.
On the other hand, five million new voters in 2012 do not have a document of identity with those characteristics.
However, the cost of obtaining the identity document is more than a hundred dollars.
In this way, the new restrictions affect the young, the minorities and the poor in a disproportionate way.

These restrictions have consequences.

Detection of prostate cancer: Should one get tested or not?
In fact, the PSA test presents false results, sometimes, in some cases, false negative or false positive results, leading to medical interventions that are useless.
It is a reason more than enough to doubt men, already reluctant, whether they should take the tests.
¿ hacerse el test o no?
We have asked for advice from two experts.
In the studies conducted in the United States, a high level of infection was detected in the samples, making it difficult to interpret those data and make firm recommendations.
On the other hand, the European study showed a difference in mortality between patients who had been tested and those who had not.
The study, with a 12-year follow-up, showed that 30% to 40% of people who do not have the test of detection will have metastasis.
I recommend a test starting at 50 years of age, or at 40 years if the father has had prostate cancer.
African-American men have a higher risk.
The key is to make a good decision once the cancer is detected.
There are aggressive cancers and other cancers that are indolent.

It is truly necessary to make sure that the patient understands the degree of risk of cancer. All options should be offered, and not necessarily the prostate cancer, in which case active monitoring should be preferred.
Today, many men who have been diagnosed with cancer are not treated, since said cancer is not aggressive nor poses a risk to their life.
In place of that, we suggest active monitoring of the disease and, if it progresses, we offer treatment.
We have decided to use more precise criteria to decide who should or should be treated.
I recommend that the test be done in any case.
However, it is important to speak with his doctor to determine whether he should take the test or not.
Movember has created, in collaboration with the International Society of Urology, a tool that allows to evaluate the pros and cons of the PSA test.
This document can be downloaded (at the moment only in English, but soon will be available in Spanish) at the following address: http://ca.movember.com/fr/mens-health/prostate-cancer-screening
To prevent the disease
Unfortunately, there is no miracle cure for cancer.
Despite the progress of the investigations, the adoption of healthy lifestyle habits remains the best way to reduce the risk of disease.
We estimate that if everyone ate well and moved sufficiently, 30% of cancers could be prevented.
"If no one smoked, that rate would rise to 50%", said André Beaulieu, spokesperson for the Canadian Cancer Society.
In contrast, we evaluate that around 10% of cancers are hereditary.
Many others are completely inexplicable.
For the Canadian Cancer Society, the fight against smoking continues to be a priority, despite the decrease in smokers.
Tobacco is linked to 85% of lung cancer cases.
It also constitutes a risk factor for other types of cancer.
It greatly harms the health of people.
"Today, 1.5 million smokers remain in Quebec", said the speaker André Beaulieu.
A hopeful data: 10 years after stopping smoking, the risk of dying of cancer is reduced by half.
The weight
Obesity also favors the appearance of the disease, according to the SCC.
The risk of breast, colon, and rectal cancer increases.
"The research shows that regular physical activity throughout life protects against breast cancer", add.
The food
The organization also recommends limiting the consumption of red meat.
In large quantities, they are at risk of developing colorectal cancer.
The products of the meat industry should be avoided.
The preservation of meat for smoking, drying or curing may lead to the formation of cancerous substances.
"They can damage the organism and lead to cancer", we are told.
The vitamins
In recent years, many scientists have studied the links between vitamin complexes and cancer.
However, at present, their investigations are not yet concluded.
According to the SCC, studies on vitamin E are contradictory.
While in one of them, a decrease in the risk of prostate cancer was observed, in another, a increase was observed.
The effect of vitamin D on cancer has not been determined with clarity.
On the other hand, M. Beaulieu insists on the importance of discussing the concerns and family history of each person with their doctor.

The Higgs boson in detail
The announcement of the probable discovery of the Higgs boson generated a great shock last summer, and it was for a reason.
It is believed that this boson is a part of the mechanism responsible for the mass of everything that exists in the universe, nothing more and nothing less.
And what is more, it is about the particle whose existence was predicted by the model: our best explanation of the nature and behavior of matter, which has not yet been observed empirically.
However, for physicists, it is not completely clear that it is Higgs.
We know for sure that there is a new particle and that it is very similar to the Higgs boson predicted by the standard model.
Moreover, new data revealed in a major physics conference in Kyoto seem to confirm that it is, although more data is still needed to be completely sure.
Nevertheless, we assume it is Higgs, since the chances of being wrong seem few. We will see what it is about.
In this great world, there is a general law that implies that two things cannot be found at the same time.
There is no way to violate that rule and do it too much, because it will end up hurting.

Although particle physics is a very complex world, it has been shown that there is a law of this type: the principle of Pauli, which states that two particles cannot occupy the same space at the same time if they are in the same "state".
The physicists classify particles into two categories.
On the one hand, we find good citizens called fermions, who obey smartly at the beginning of Pauli.
And there are also the anarchists, a group of anarchists who do not respect anything or at least not this principle, meaning that they may be in the same place at the same time.

According to the web page The Particle Adventure of Berkeley, which is extraordinary, the particles are divided into two groups: the mesons, which we will not discuss here, and the "particles of force", with which the natural forces are related and in which the Higgs particle is, in some way, related.
These bosons, as we can highlight here, are not the exotic creatures that we could believe.
In fact, if he manages to read this article, it is due to a extraordinary particle: the photon or the " particle of light" that acts as a " messenger" of electromagnetic force.
In fact, when a charged particle accelerates or changes direction, it disrupts the electromagnetic field in that environment; a little like when we throw a stone into a pond.
In this " disorder ", a electromagnetic wave (of light, infrared, etc.) is born, and this wave is nothing but a photon; that is, one of the bosons " carriers of force".
The most stable field
The same happens with the Higgs boson, with the difference that it is another field, the Higgs field, which needs to be "ordered" for this boson to appear.

Now, the Higgs field is much more stable than the electromagnetic field. To activate it, one needs to reach extremely high energies, just like a frozen lake in which only a thick rock can slide across the surface.
Therefore, a huge particle accelerator, such as the Large Hadron Collider (the great particle accelerator is a 27 km ring!) is needed to reach such levels of energy.
The analogy with the electromagnetic field is a new tool that explains the relationship between the Higgs and mass.
In fact, not all particles nor all materials interact with the electromagnetic field.
Some, like magnets, do this, but others, like a piece of paper, do not: a piece of paper, for example, does not remain stuck to the door of a refrigerator.
And in the same way, not all particles interact with the Higgs field: those that do have mass, while the rest (in fact, the photon, by the way) do not.
In conclusion, what can all those investigations contribute? asks Mrs. Plamondon.
For science, this serves to verify the validity of the standard model (MS), and allows physicists to examine the differences between observations and predictions of the MS.
On the other hand, many desire that the smallest difference could open a door to a new physics that covers certain holes in the model.
This, in fact, has enormous deficiencies, such as not proposing any explanation relative to the gravity (¡ups!) or the dark matter (¡otro ups!), which makes up 80% of the universe (¡another ups!).
However, we have not found such differences in the CERN until now.
Consequences
The consequences of these investigations on our daily life are difficult to predict, but we do not believe that we are wrong in saying that it will have none.
For the sake of seeing: in the 60s, the pioneers of laser in laboratories did not expect at all the revolution that their work would provoke.
They saw scientific applications, but nothing more.

In fact, as the physicist Willard Boyle, who worked in Bell Laboratories, where the laser was developed in 1960, and who made the first continuous laser (the first were pulsed) in 1962, at first the laser was considered a "lab equipment".
Imagine...
And also, the applications may come from any of the instruments that surround the research.

A Constitution with a knife in Egypt
It is a new double or nothing with the President Mohammed Morsi.
While Egypt is more divided than ever in terms of the constitutional declaration, which grants him provisional powers, he decided to play the whole for the whole.
The surprise of the Wednesday when he announced that the Constituent Assembly would vote his final text the next day.
Just a week ago, the Head of State had given two more months to this Assembly to finish its work.
And almost two years have passed since Egypt has used a provisional text, several times revised, which weakens the institutional stability and leads to judicial entanglements.
This new initiative has only increased the fracture in the country.
For his opponents, the president persists in his "autocratic delirium" and continues "betraying his word" and "stepping on the right".
On the part of its supporters, it is assured that this is a measure to end the institutional and political crisis more quickly and to accelerate the transition process.
In the next 15 days, a referendum should be organized.
A very short time that forces the Brothers to resign from their project of explaining the text, article by article, to the Egyptians.
For the president, it is also a form of restoring popular and democratic legitimacy while the controversy is causing havoc throughout the country.
Mohammed Morsi seems convinced that the Egyptians will vote for him, as he stated in an interview with the American weekly magazine Time.

Considering that this resource has been voted on with great speed, it contains an ultimatum for the Egyptian people: "Vote my text or I will keep the full powers", powers that supposedly will end with the adoption of the Constitution.
It was in this strange atmosphere in which 85 members of this Constituent Assembly, mostly Muslim, voted the text yesterday.
Most of the liberals did not attend the call.
In mid-November, a little before the constitutional declaration, they had closed the door because they thought they could not make their views prevail.
The representatives of human rights, religious minorities, and civil society made the same.
In order to achieve the necessary quorum, 11 substitute members were added hastily this morning.
Some of them are very close to the Muslim Brothers.
As expected, the articles passed unanimously.

To the commentators, it is amusing that one of the few discrepancies of the day has been expressed practically at the time of prayer, so much so that several members of the committee arrived at the conclusion that the clock of the Constituent was wrong.
The text, which was still being voted on yesterday afternoon, consists of 234 articles.
Article 2, the subject of all eyes, is finally identical to the one in the 1971 Constitution, which stipulated that "the principles of Sharia constitute the main source of law."

The Salafist parties, for whom the establishment of Islamic law is a fundamental claim, hoped that they could replace "the principles" with "the rules", which would have allowed a more strict application.
For the Islamic group, that this article has not been modified is a guarantee of their good will and respect for the other components of Egyptian society.
The liberals call him hypocrisy and consider that it is not more than a publicity stunt.
According to them, the Islamization of the Constitution is done through other articles.
They refer, especially to Article 220, which grants the Al-Azhar University a consultative role, particularly for anyone who has to confirm their compliance with the laws of Sharia.
